Target Endpoints (The 'Heavy' Paths).bottleneck: Massive ORM overhead. Performs three joinedloads (Delivery.order -> Order.restaurant, Order.customer, Order.items) without pagination or index limits.
Heavy write transaction. Creates an Order, multiple OrderItems, and auto-generates a Delivery record within a single transactional scope. Calculates subtotals repeatedly.

Multi-tenant leakage risk. Queries all restaurants owned by a user, extracts their IDs into a Python list, and filters `Order.restaurant_id.in_(target_ids)`. Subject to severe degradation if an owner has many restaurants/orders.

Simulated external latency (`await asyncio.sleep(random.uniform(0.5, 2.0))`). Under high concurrency, this will rapidly exhaust the Uvicorn worker limits or PostgreSQL connection pool while waiting for the sleep to complete.
Complex dynamic filtering (`ilike` wildcard searches on name, description, city). Table scans highly probable depending on Postgres index configurations.

Authentication & State.mechanism: Clients POST credentials to `/api/v1/auth/login`. Server hashes password via `passlib` (bcrypt), returns `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
Authentication & State.vu_bypass_strategy: VUs must simulate the login sequence once per session to acquire the Bearer token, or pre-seed a static list of valid tokens in Redis/CSV for the VUs to round-robin, bypassing the expensive bcrypt hashing step during the actual load test.

Infrastructure Bottlenecks.db_connection_pool: SQLAlchemy engine initialized with `pool_size=10, max_overflow=20` (in `backend/app/db/base.py`). This strictly caps concurrent database connections at 30. Any requests beyond 30 concurrent DB hits will queue and eventually timeout.
Infrastructure Bottlenecks.caching: Redis is used for ObservationLogs and Injection coordination, but there is ZERO caching applied to domain entities (Restaurants, Menus, Orders). Every GET request hits Postgres.
Infrastructure Bottlenecks.sync_io_in_async: SQLAlchemy ORM queries are executed synchronously. Despite FastAPI being async, these DB calls will block the thread pool, leading to event loop starvation.
